jobs.description: About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world. Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you. Job Description Visa, Inc. is seeking a Stock Plan Analyst to join our Global Equity Program team, based in Austin, TX or Atlanta, GA. This role is responsible for the day-to-day administration of Visa’s global equity programs, including all aspects of equity recordkeeping, reporting, and reconciliation. The Stock Plan Analyst ensures the accuracy and integrity of all equity data within stock plan systems and works closely with employees and cross-functional partners to deliver a high-quality equity administration experience. Administer and support multiple global equity plans, including Performance Stock, Restricted Stock, Stock Units, Non-Qualified Stock Options, and Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP). Process equity transactions such as grants, vesting, exercises, lapses, and cancellations, and support payroll and tax reporting related to equity events. Maintain equity records across third-party stock plan administration platforms (experience with Bank of America/Merrill Employer Sponsor platform preferred). Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Tax, Payroll, Accounting, Audit, Financial Reporting, and Human Resources. Support insider trading compliance programs, including monitoring blackout periods and trading activity. Assist with SEC filings, 10b5-1 plans, stock ownership guideline compliance, and Section 16 reporting (Forms 3, 4, and 5), including proxy-related disclosures. Coordinate with transfer agents and third-party administrators to ensure timely settlement of trades and reconciliation of DWAC and transfer agent activity. Maintain stock plan documentation in support of internal controls and SOX compliance. Prepare and support employee communications related to equity compensation programs. Respond to employee inquiries and coordinate with internal teams and external vendors to resolve issues effectively. Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls, and employee experiences related to equity programs. Perform other duties related to the administration and ongoing enhancement of the equity programs. Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. Qualifications Basic Qualifications: 2 or more years of work experience with a bachelor’s degree or an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD, or PhD). Preferred Qualifications: 3 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or more than 2 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD)​. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field, or an advanced degree (e.g., MBA, JD, or similar). Minimum 2 years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience with an advanced degree. Minimum 3 years of experience administering equity compensation programs at a public company. Experience supporting global equity programs and multiple equity award types. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with HRIS platforms. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Customer-service mindset with excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Exceptionally detail-oriented, resourceful, and able to thrive in a fast-paced environment. Demonstrated ability to identify and implement process improvements. Certified Equity Professional (CEP) designation is a plus. Information for US Applicants For roles located in the US, the estimated salary range for this position is $98,700 to $153,200 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. In addition, this position may be eligible for bonus and equity.Visa has a comprehensive benefits package for which this position may be eligible that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness Program. Work Hours Varies upon the needs of the department. Travel Requirements This position requires travel 5-10% of the time. Mental/Physical Requirements This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, frequently operate standard office equipment, such as telephones and computers. Visa is an EEO Employer Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protect veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

jobs.description: This is where your work makes a difference. At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond. Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results. Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride. Your role at Baxter At Baxter, we are deeply connected by our mission. No matter your role, your work makes a positive impact on people around the world. You'll feel a sense of purpose throughout the organization, as we know our work improves outcomes for millions of patients. As the Senior Trade and Customs Analyst, you will play a critical role in ensuring Baxter's global trade operations remain compliant, efficient, and strategically optimized. You will serve as a subject matter expert supporting U.S. and international import and export activities while helping Baxter navigate complex customs regulations, trade programs, and supply chain security requirements. This is where your expertise in customs compliance, trade programs, and cross-functional collaboration helps keep critical healthcare products moving across borders safely, efficiently, and compliantly, ultimately supporting Baxter's mission to save and sustain lives. In this role, you will partner closely with logistics, procurement, manufacturing, distribution, finance, legal, customs brokers, freight forwarders, and government agencies to manage compliance obligations, reduce trade-related risk, and identify opportunities for operational and duty cost optimization. Success will be measured through regulatory compliance, operational excellence, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement of Baxter's global trade programs. Your team The Global Trade Compliance team is responsible for supporting the compliant movement of products and materials across international borders, helping ensure patients receive the critical therapies and medical products they depend on. Through partnership with internal partners and external agencies, the team safeguards Baxter's supply chain while supporting business growth and operational continuity. Our team fosters a collaborative, solutions-oriented environment where expertise, accountability, and continuous improvement are highly valued. Team members work closely across functions and regions to solve complex trade challenges, support strategic initiatives, and drive compliance excellence. At Baxter, we invest in our employees through programs and benefits that support both personal and professional growth, including paid volunteer time, resources for working parents and caregivers, matching charitable contributions, professional development opportunities, and comprehensive health and wellness programs. What you'll be doing Support daily import and export operations and ensure compliant cross-border movement of products and materials. Monitor customs clearance activities, resolve shipment delays and compliance issues, and collaborate with customs brokers and logistics providers. Ensure accurate customs declarations, tariff classifications, customs valuation determinations, and country of origin assessments. Support and maintain Baxter's trade compliance programs, including CTPAT, Importer Self-Assessment (ISA), Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ), and Free Trade Agreement (FTA) initiatives. Conduct post-entry reviews, compliance testing, self-assessments, audits, and corrective action activities to maintain regulatory compliance. Manage FTA qualification and certification processes, perform origin analyses, and identify duty savings opportunities through trade preference programs. Support FTZ administration activities, including inventory control, reporting, reconciliations, admissions, withdrawals, and audit preparation. Analyze trade data, duty spend, broker performance metrics, and compliance trends to develop reports, dashboards, and recommendations that improve operational performance and reduce risk. What you'll bring 3+ years of experience in global trade, customs compliance, import/export operations, or a related field. Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college/university preferred. Experience using BI Publisher for reporting, data extraction, and analysis. Strong knowledge of U.S. Customs regulations, customs entry processes, and international trade requirements. Experience supporting CTPAT, ISA, FTZ, and Free Trade Agreement (FTA) programs. Knowledge of HTS classification, customs valuation, country of origin determination, and duty mitigation strategies. Experience working with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and government agencies. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills. Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) certification. Experience within medical device, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or other highly regulated industries. Familiarity with SAP, JDE, GME, ACE, or other trade management systems. Knowledge of export controls, sanctions compliance, and denied party screening processes. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Scopely Explore is looking for an Executive Producer for Pikmin Bloom to join its Leadership Team and help shape the future of one of the world’s leading location-based live service games.
The Executive Producer owns execution across the game organization, enabling teams to consistently deliver exceptional player experiences through operational excellence, cross-functional leadership, and predictable execution. Working closely with the General Manager and functional leaders, this role establishes production practices, operating rhythms, and organizational processes that allow globally distributed teams to operate as One Team.
The Executive Producer owns execution across the game organization, enabling teams to consistently deliver exceptional player experiences through operational excellence, cross-functional leadership, and predictable execution. Working closely with the General Manager and functional leaders, this role establishes production practices, operating rhythms, and organizational processes that allow globally distributed teams—primarily across Japan and the United States—to operate as One Team.
From long-term roadmap planning to LiveOps execution, the Executive Producer ensures that strategy is translated into clear plans, teams remain aligned, risks are proactively managed, and the organization consistently delivers high-quality outcomes.
What You Will Do
Lead planning and execution across the game organization, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery of the product roadmap and LiveOps.
Partner closely with the General Manager and Leadership Team to translate the game’s vision and strategy into actionable roadmaps, milestones, and operating plans.
Establish world-class production practices, operating rhythms, and planning processes that improve transparency, predictability, and execution.
Create and foster a One Team mindset across Design, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Analytics, and external partners.
Build strong alignment across globally distributed teams, primarily across Japan and the United States, while maintaining efficient communication and clear ownership.
Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with key external partners, including major IP partners such as Nintendo, ensuring effective collaboration and alignment throughout development and live operations.
Develop and grow a high-performing Production organization that serves as a force multiplier for the entire game team.
Maintain a comprehensive understanding of the overall project, proactively identifying risks, removing organizational blockers, and driving timely decisions.
Ensure production supports player-centric development through iterative planning, playtesting, and continuous improvement.
Drive scalable production processes that support the long-term operation of a global live service game.
Provide clear visibility into project health, execution risks, and mitigation plans to senior leadership.
AI-Enabled Operational Excellence: Champion the adoption of AI-powered workflows that improve planning, communication, documentation, risk management, and production visibility. Continuously identify opportunities to automate routine work, accelerate execution, and increase the effectiveness of globally distributed teams.
Required in-office 3 days per week on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday
What We're Looking For
Proven experience leading production for a successful live service mobile game.
Demonstrated track record establishing production practices that improve execution across cross-functional teams.
Experience leading globally distributed development teams, including collaboration with external partners, including major IP partners.
Strong understanding of software development methodologies and modern game production practices.
Excellent organizational, analytical, and communication skills.
Exceptional ability to influence, align, and lead without direct authority.
Strong judgment with the ability to identify risks early and drive effective mitigation.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement AI-native workflows, custom tools, and automation that measurably improve planning, execution, and overall team efficiency.
Passion for building high-performing teams and healthy organizational culture.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both English and Japanese
Plus if…
Experience leading production on a globally operated free-to-play mobile game.
Experience partnering with major entertainment or gaming IP holders.
Experience operating games with seasonal LiveOps, experimentation, and continuous content delivery.
Experience building or scaling Production organizations through periods of significant growth.
Familiarity with geolocation-based or outdoor gaming experiences.
Deep appreciation for player-first product development and long-term live service operations.
Please ensure that the résumé/CV you attach is written in English.

jobs.description: AWS Hardware Engineering Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global compute systems. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering team creates compute and storage server designs for Amazon’s web services. Our engineers work with leading edge technologies, solve challenging problems, influence the industry’s roadmaps, and develop new and unique solutions that are ahead of the pack. We work in an environment that fosters innovation and creativity. We encourage and invest in new directions and new ideas that will serve our customers better.
